data.name: Sidram
data.gender_notes: Sidram is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Sidh means 'achieved' and Rama means 'auspicious' or 'virtuous'. This name signifies one who has achieved auspiciousness or virtue. The name Sidram carries the meaning “Auspicious, Virtuous” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Sidram usually hope their child will grow to embody auspicious, virtuous and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Sidram is a spiritual name that represents one's inner strength and wisdom, as well as their ability to overcome challenges and obstacles.
data.etymology: Sidram belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Auspicious, Virtuous.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sidram total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: The name Sidram holds a significant place in Hindu mythology as it is associated with Lord Rama, one of the most revered deities in Hinduism. The name inspires devotion, virtue, and a sense of achievement.
data.spiritual_significance: Sidram represents the attainment of self-realization and spiritual purity. It signifies the journey of an individual towards acquiring virtues and ultimately reaching a state of enlightenment. The name encourages one to strive towards inner and outer evolution and rest in the auspiciousness and grace of the Divine.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Sidram is a name derived from the Sanskrit words 'Shidh' (intelligence) and 'Ram' (God Vishnu). It symbolizes the pure and intelligent soul, always connected to the divine consciousness of Lord Vishnu. This name evokes wisdom, knowledge, and spiritual growth.

historical_references.reference: The legend of Sidra or Sidram is mentioned in the Skanda Purana, a major Hindu scripture. Sidra is believed to be a devotee of Lord Subramanya, also known as Lord Kartikeya. According to the legend, Sidra was a sage who performed severe penance to please Lord Subramanya.
historical_references.time_period: Skanda Purana - Unknown, but likely written between 6th and 10th centuries CE

historical_references.reference: Another reference to Sidram can be found in the 12th-century CE work, Aadipurana, a Tamil classic in the Skanda Purana Cycle. In this text, Sidram is depicted as a devotee of Lord Murugan, another name for Lord Subramanya. He is believed to have attained the grace of Lord Murugan through his devotion and penance.
